locales._locale_comment: One Portuguese locale, written in Brazilian Portuguese, matching the app's pt-BR catalog and its one-locale decision. The code is bare `pt` because the registry has no regional codes and Portugal reaches this locale by base-language fallback, exactly as a Portugal device reaches the app's pt-BR catalog. hreflang is `pt` so both markets resolve here; html_lang is `pt-BR` because that is the variety actually written.

locales._locale_comment: Taiwan-standard Traditional Chinese, matching the app's zh-Hant catalog. The code is not a bare `zh` because Chinese splits by script rather than by region: a Simplified reader served Traditional text is reading the wrong script, not a regional variant, and the app already shipped a bug where a base-code `zh` table served Simplified names to a Traditional interface. zh-Hans is planned separately and must never fall back to this locale.

locales._locale_comment: Mainland-standard Simplified Chinese, matching the app's zh-Hans catalog. Kept a separate locale from zh-Hant rather than a regional variant of it: Chinese splits by script, so a Simplified reader served Traditional text is reading the wrong script. The two Chinese locales never fall back to each other, only to English. og_locale is zh_CN because Open Graph requires a territory and Simplified's largest readership is there; it is a language signal, not a storefront claim, and there is deliberately no mainland App Store listing.
